howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.intro: Guinea Pig Monitor looks after your guinea pigs' health while you are not watching. This is how it works, step by step.

mark.title: Each guinea pig wears a color mark
mark.text: You register each guinea pig with its name, its breed and the color of the mark on its back. That color is how it is recognized.

watch.title: The cage watches and listens
watch.text: A camera watches the guinea pigs, a microphone listens for squeals and a scale weighs the cage.

analyse.title: Artificial intelligence analyses it
analyse.text: Every minute, an Amazon Bedrock vision model measures how much each guinea pig moves and how often it visits the feeder, and sends it to the system.

panel.title: You see it on the dashboard
panel.text: Here you see the status of each guinea pig and the alerts. When you take care of one, mark it as reviewed.

admin.title: For admins
admin.intro: Besides your cages, you look after the whole system from Administration. Each part has its own tab.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.text: You see how many cages, guinea pigs and open alerts each account has and when it last sent data. You can make someone an admin (it asks twice), remove that role, or disable and enable an account without deleting its guinea pigs.

rules.title: Health rules
rules.text: You decide when a guinea pig goes to observed, alert or critical and when the weight warns. Each field shows its range and default; it applies on saving.

texts.title: Alert texts and assistant
texts.text: You change what the breeder reads on each alert and how many questions each account can ask Cuchi. "Back to the defaults" puts everything back.

catalog.title: Catalog
catalog.text: You add or hide breeds and mark colors. A hidden option stays on the guinea pigs that already use it.

logs.title: Logs
logs.text: The action log keeps what you changed and whether it worked; the AI log shows what the AI analysed in each cage and the notes it wrote.

help.title: How do I connect the camera?
help.tapo1: Set up the camera with the Tapo app and connect it to the same Wi-Fi as the laptop. Use a 2.4 GHz network: the C200 does not work on 5 GHz.
help.tapo2: In the Tapo app tap the camera → Settings (gear) → Advanced settings → Camera account. Create a username and password. It is not your TP-Link account.
help.tapo3: In Settings → Device info, copy the IP address (for example 192.168.1.60).
help.tapo4: So the IP does not change, reserve it in your router (fixed IP or "DHCP reservation"). If you don't know how, ask whoever set up your internet.
help.tapo5: Video quality: keep "Low (for slow laptops)" if the laptop is slow or you are not sure. "High" looks better, but it asks more of the laptop.
help.tapo6: Here choose "Tapo camera (Wi-Fi)", type the IP, username and password, and tap "Save and test".
help.tapo7: In a few seconds you will see "Camera connected" or what to check.
help.phone1: Open IP Webcam on the phone and tap "Start server".
help.phone2: Copy the IP and port shown at the bottom of the screen (for example 192.168.1.50:8080).
help.phone3: With the phone on the same Wi-Fi as the laptop, choose "Phone with IP Webcam", type the IP and port and tap "Save and test".

usb.hint: Run this check on the computer connected to the Arduino.
usb.checking: Select the Arduino port. Waiting for USB data…

usb.silent: Port opened but no data arrived. Check the sketch and its 115200 baud rate.
usb.valid: A stable weight arrived over USB. If it is missing from the dashboard, check the forwarding service and connected cage.
usb.unstable: The scale sends grams over USB but the weight is still unstable.
usb.negative: The scale is sending negative grams. Check tare and calibration.
usb.unknown: Unrecognized USB data. Check the sketch and baud rate.
usb.lost: Communication with the USB port was interrupted.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what data the Guinea Pig Health Monitor collects, what it is used for and what you can do with it. It is an academic project; even so, we handle your data with care and follow Colombia's personal data protection law (Ley 1581 de 2012).

who.title: Who is responsible
who.text: The student team that builds the Guinea Pig Health Monitor is responsible for the data stored in the app. You can reach us through the system administrators.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.text:
• Your account: name, username, email, a profile photo if you upload one, and your password stored encrypted (never in plain text).
• If you sign in with Google: the name and email Google verified.
• Your guinea pigs and cages: names, color marks, photos, weights, alerts and health history.
• The cage devices: scale readings and the images and sounds sent for analysis.
• What you write to the help assistant.

use.title: What we use it for
use.text: To create and protect your account (including the verification code we email you), show the state of your guinea pigs, warn you about alerts and answer your questions in the assistant. We do not sell your data or use it for advertising.

providers.title: Who it is shared with
providers.text: Only with the services the app needs to work: Amazon Web Services hosts the server and the database; Amazon Bedrock analyses the images and sounds of the cage and answers in the assistant; Google handles Google sign-in; and Gmail sends the emails with the codes. No other account can see your cages or guinea pigs.

cookies.title: Cookies and storage
cookies.text: We use secure (HttpOnly) cookies only to keep you signed in. Your preferences, like language or theme, are saved in your browser. We do not use advertising or tracking cookies.

keep.title: How long we keep it
keep.text: While your account is active. If you disable it, you can no longer sign in and your data stops being shown. Alerts you delete are removed for good.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.text: You can see and correct your data in My account, change your photo and password, delete alerts and guinea pigs, and disable your account. You can also ask the administrators what data we hold or to delete it.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.text: If we change this policy we will update the date above. If the change is important, we will tell you in the app.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: These terms govern the use of the Guinea Pig Health Monitor. Please read them before creating your account.

accept.title: Acceptance
accept.text: By creating an account or using the app you accept these terms and the Privacy policy. If you do not agree, do not use the app.

service.title: What the service offers
service.text: A tool to follow the health of your guinea pigs: the state of each one, alerts, history, weight and a help assistant. It is an academic project offered free and as is, and it may change or stop being available.

account.title: Your account
account.text: Give true details and keep your password and the codes we send you safe. You are responsible for what is done with your account. Tell us if you think someone got in without your permission.

use.title: Acceptable use
use.text: Do not try to get into other people's accounts or cages, attack or overload the service, or upload illegal or offensive content. We may disable accounts that do.

demo.title: Demo accounts
demo.text: The demo buttons open shared accounts to try the app. Do not store personal data in them: anyone can see them.

health.title: Not a substitute for a vet
health.text: Alerts and assistant answers are generated automatically and can be wrong. They are a help, not a diagnosis: if you have any doubt about a guinea pig's health, see a vet.

liability.title: Liability
liability.text: We are not liable for losses or damage resulting from failures of the service, of the cage devices, or from decisions taken only on the app's information.

end.title: Ending use
end.text: You can stop using the app and disable your account at any time. We may suspend an account that breaks these terms.

changes.title: Changes and governing law
changes.text: We may update these terms; the date above shows the latest version. They are governed by the laws of the Republic of Colombia.
